# bWalletX for Android

The full bWalletX wallet on your Android phone or tablet. Your keys stay on your device.

[Download APK (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-android-5.1.76.apk)

It isn't on Google Play yet, so install it by hand:

- Tap Download APK on your Android device.

- If Android asks, allow your browser to install unknown apps (Settings › Apps › your browser › Install unknown apps).

- Open `bwalletx-android-5.1.76.apk` and tap Install.

- Open bWalletX and create or restore your wallet.

Updating from an older version? Install over the top and your wallet stays. If Android says the app can't be updated, write down your 12 words first, then uninstall and reinstall.

Version 5.1.76 beta · 18.2 MB · Android 7+ · SHA-256 710bcb1811682d29bbba58f86a64f439fccde6508b67cb57a79535e52c0aa0ac

Also: [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension) · [Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

# Buy BSV in bWalletX

Open the wallet and the gold Buy BSV card is right at the top, with today’s price. Tap it to buy with a card or bank, or to receive BSV from an exchange or a friend.

Buy BSV$20.26 per BSV

The price on the card is live and updates every minute. You’ll also find the card under the BSV price chart, and a Get BSV button on your BSV row while it’s empty.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## How it works

### Tap Buy BSV

The gold card at the top of your wallet opens the Get BSV sheet.

### Pick how

Pay with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank. Or receive from an exchange, another wallet or a friend.

### It lands in your wallet

Your BSV shows up in your wallet, in dollars. Ready to send, mint or trade.

## Ways to get BSV

### From an exchange or another wallet

bWalletX shows your BSV address and QR code. Send from wherever your BSV is now.

### From a friend

Share your $name or paymail. They send to it and it arrives in seconds.

### With a card or bank

Pick a provider in the sheet. It opens in the wallet’s browser. Copy your address from Receive and paste it there.

The card and bank providers in the sheet today:

- Ramp · Apple Pay, Google Pay, card or bank

- BSV Association · buy page run by the BSV Association

- Guardarian · card or bank transfer

- ChangeNOW · card, many currencies

- Alchemy Pay · card, Apple Pay, Google Pay

- Onramper · compares several card providers

- cex.io · card; needs an exchange account

### Good to know

These providers are independent companies, not bWalletX. They check your ID and set their own fees and limits, and what’s on offer depends on where you live. bWalletX never holds your money: you pay the provider, and the BSV goes straight to your own wallet. We’re working on buying with Ramp fully inside the app, with your address filled in for you. It isn’t live yet.

## What can I do with BSV?

### [Mint something](https://bwalletx.com/mint)

Put your art, music or tickets on chain. A photo costs a fraction of a cent.

### [Get PNEEs](https://bwalletx.com/pnees)

Digital cents on BSV, backed by BSV locked in public vaults.

### [Trade on the Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange)

Buy and sell tokens, priced in dollars.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX Exchange

In bWalletX the Market is an exchange: buy and sell tokens and NFTs directly between wallets. bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Need BSV to start? [Buy BSV in bWalletX →](https://bwalletx.com/buy) with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank, or from a friend.

Browse→Buy→Sell

## What's on it

### Tokens and Social

Every BSV-21 token, including people's $HANDLE tokens. Holding one gets you into its chat room.

### Music, video, images, documents

1Sat Ordinals NFTs, filtered for safety. Play music and video you own in the wallet.

### Sell yours

List your tokens and NFTs at your own price from the wallet, and cancel any time.

### Strategies

Programs for your [agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agent), sold as encrypted NFTs. [See what’s for sale →](https://bwalletx.com/exchange/strategies)

## Exchange or Market?

bWalletX ExchangebWallet Market

WhereAndroid, Chrome, webApp Store, Google Play

Browse tokens, music, video, images, documentsYesYes

Buy and sell, wallet to walletYesNo, browse only

List your own tokens and NFTs for saleYesNo

Social: people's $HANDLE tokensBuy, sell, join their roomsBrowse

Strategies for your agents[Yes](https://bwalletx.com/exchange/strategies)No

Why two? App stores only allow trading from licensed exchanges, so the App Store and Google Play edition, bWallet, lets you browse. The full edition, bWalletX, trades. The X is for exchange.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)[Buy BSV →](https://bwalletx.com/buy)[bWallet Market (App Store) →](https://www.bwallet.space/market)

Trades settle on chain between wallets. Tokens and NFTs can lose all value.

# Exchange › Strategies

Programs your agent account runs, written and sold by bWalletX users. Each one is an encrypted NFT: read the spec here, buy it in bWalletX, test it on live prices first.

Compare the spec→Buy in bWalletX→Test on live prices

Strategies are programs written and sold by users. bWalletX doesn’t review, rate or recommend them. The wallet enforces each strategy’s own limits before anything is signed.

## For sale now

Loading strategies…

## Free examples

Four starter strategies you can download and load straight into an agent account: [Slow accumulator](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/slow-accumulator.json), [Dip buyer](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/dip-buyer.json), [Take profit](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/take-profit.json) and [Allowance](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/allowance.json). More on [Strategies](https://bwalletx.com/strategies).

## Sell yours

In bWalletX, load your strategy into an agent account, then tap Sell: fill in the spec, set a dollar price and how many copies, and publish. Buyers pay you directly. The format is in the [strategy spec](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/spec).

# bWalletX for Chrome and Brave

The full bWalletX wallet in Chrome's side panel, and a wallet websites like TokenBlaster can connect to. Your keys stay in the extension.

[Download for Chrome (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.1.76.zip)
[Download for Brave (beta) ↓](https://bwalletx.com/download/bwalletx-extension-5.1.76.zip)

It isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet, so install it by hand:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.1.76.zip`.

- Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

## Brave

Same extension, same file. Brave runs Chrome extensions, so:

- Unzip `bwalletx-extension-5.1.76.zip`.

- Open `brave://extensions` in Brave.

- Turn on Developer mode (top right).

- Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.

- Pin bWalletX from the puzzle-piece menu, click it, and create or restore your wallet.

# bWalletX features

One non-custodial BSV wallet for money, names, tokens, rooms, media and apps. Your keys never leave your device.

[Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[iPhone · web app](https://bwalletx.com/iphone)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[Web](https://web.bwalletx.com)

bWalletX only in bWalletX (Android, Chrome, web). Everything else is also in [bWallet](https://www.bwallet.space) from the App Store and Google Play.

## 💰Wallet

### BSV, priced in dollars

Balances and prices in USD; you pay in sats. Live price chart.

### Buy BSV

Buy with a card from inside the wallet, in dollars, sent straight to your address. [How](https://bwalletx.com/buy).

### Send to names

Pay a paymail like `name@bwalletx.com` instead of a long address.

### Tokens and NFTs

Hold, send and receive BSV-21 tokens and 1Sat Ordinals, with a separate ordinals address.

### Restore from anywhere

12 words are enough. Import from Yours, Panda, RelayX or Twetch, a private key or a backup file.

### Sweep another wallet

Pull funds in from any 12/24-word wallet, scanning its addresses for you.

### Find lost tokens

Recover purchases and tokens that didn't show up, and heal indexing.

### Several accounts

Keep separate accounts, each with its own name.

### bCreditsbWalletX

Top up credits for bCorp apps from the Wallet tab.

## 🪪Names and identity

### Your own paymail

Claim `yourname@bwalletx.com` and receive to it.

### Verified X and Google namesbWalletX

Sign in with X or Google for a verified `name.x` or `name.gmail`, with your photo.

### Every name visible

Settings lists every name your wallet receives at, with one-tap unlink.

### Profile and avatar

An avatar and display name that follow you into chat and the market.

### Signed issuer statements

Every token you mint carries a statement signed by your identity, so anyone can check who made it.

### Verified identity (optional)

KYC through bit-sign, where you choose what to reveal.

## ✨Make things

### Your personal tokenbWalletX

Mint a $HANDLE token named after you in one tap. Its icon is your profile picture.

### Mint tokens

Create BSV-21 tokens with your own supply, icon and name.

### Mint NFTs

Inscribe images, music and video as 1Sat Ordinals.

### TicketsbWalletX

Mint a ticket token; sending one invites someone into your room.

## 💬Friends and social

### Token roomsbWalletX

Hold the token, join the room. Every token gets a chat room; its owner sets the rules.

### Friends

Your address book: message, call or pay anyone, and see their token and room.

### Direct messages

Private chats with your contacts.

### Voice and video calls

Call friends straight from the wallet. Turn your camera on or off mid-call and flip between front and back.

### BountiesbWalletX

Post paid tasks in a token room and pay out from your wallet when they're done.

### One feed for BSV social

Twetch, Treechat and bChat posts in one timeline, with full-size images, source badges and bookmarks. Twetch first by default.

### Lock to like

Back a post by time-locking your own BSV against it, plus a most-locked leaderboard.

### Push notifications

DMs always reach you; groups only when you're mentioned, or set each room's bell to All, Mentions or Off. Previews off by default, plus quiet hours. On iPhone, Android, the web and Chrome. [More](https://bwalletx.com/push).

### $b in every room

Type `/b` in any chat and bWalletX's own assistant answers there, day or night. `/b` on its own lists the commands.

### bWallet Lounge

The community room on [bChat](https://www.bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE): ask questions, meet other users, talk to the team.

## 📈Market and media

### The exchangebWalletX

Buy and sell tokens and NFTs wallet to wallet, including every $HANDLE token and verified X accounts.

### Browse the market

Explore tokens and NFTs, filtered for safety.

### SellbWalletX

List your tokens and NFTs at your own price from the wallet.

### Safety filter

Always-on filter for unsafe content in the market; your own items blur instead.

### Media player

Play music and video ordinals you own, with a mini player.

### SharesbWalletX

See company share listings in the market.

## 🧩Apps and websites

### bApps store

A built-in store of Bitcoin apps, one tap away. Desktop- or phone-sized.

### Browser

Open BSV apps inside the wallet; they can ask it to pay or sign.

### Connect to websites

A BRC-100 wallet sites can connect to. [For developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers).

### Pair by QR

Scan a site's QR with your phone to connect it, and see or remove paired sites.

### b agent

A help assistant with your own AI key, or pay per message from the wallet.

## 👻Agents

### Agent accountsbWalletX

Give an AI its own account with a budget and a daily cap. Each one gets a little pixel ghost in its own colour, on the card and as its avatar. [How it works](https://bwalletx.com/agent).

### Stop allbWalletX

One tap freezes every agent; a stopped agent can't spend. Every action is logged in dollars.

### bAgentsbWalletX

The ghost house: see all your agents, their balances and spending today, and stop or resume them. At [agents.bwalletx.com](https://agents.bwalletx.com).

### CLI and MCP

Pair a computer or Claude to an agent account with `npx bwalletx`. [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) · [MCP](https://bwalletx.com/mcp).

## 🔐Security

### Non-custodial

Keys are created and stored on your device. We never see them.

### Approve every request

Nothing is signed or paid without your tap; set a one-tap limit for small payments.

### Face ID and fingerprint

Unlock with biometrics on your phone.

### Strong passwords

Generate a strong password and change it anytime.

### Delete your account

Remove your paymail, profile and messages from our servers whenever you like.

Some features are still in beta and vary by platform. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Your $name is your token

In bWalletX, one name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 1. Handles

Your handle is a paymail: an address that looks like an email, such as `yourname@bwalletx.com`. People send you money, tokens and messages to your name instead of a long string of letters and numbers. Claiming one is free.

A wallet has one main name. It can keep older names that still receive, and Settings › Identity lists every one of them, so nothing receives for you without you knowing. You can unlink any of them.

## 2. Sign in with X or Google

Prove who you are, and your name is verified:

### X → `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with X and you get your exact X username, marked as verified. Nobody else can claim it.

### Google → `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with a Gmail address and you get a matching verified name.

Your X or Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture too. bWalletX never sees your X or Google password, and your keys never leave your device. If a wallet has a verified name, that name is its main name, token and room. Want a different identity? Add another account.

## 3. Tokenised handles

Turn your name into a token in one tap: $HANDLE for handle@bwalletx.com. It's a BSV-21 token on the Bitcoin SV blockchain, with a fixed supply that starts in your wallet. Its icon is your profile picture.

Anyone can copy a ticker, so bWalletX checks every token's signed creator record. Only the token actually made by that name's owner gets the check mark. Copycats don't.

Personal tokens are social tokens: they're for access and fun, not investments. They don't pay dividends.

## 4. The market

Every user token can be bought and sold in the bWalletX Market. List some of yours for sale at your own price, or buy someone else's to get into their room. Trades settle directly between wallets on chain; bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Before a token shows up in other wallets and the Market, its creator pays a one-off indexing deposit to the 1Sat indexer. It's a prepaid balance that pays for the token's transfers, not a fee to bWalletX.

## 5. Chat rooms

Every user token has a chat room. Hold the token, join the room. Inviting someone is as simple as sending them one token.

The room's owner sets its rules: how many tokens you need to hold to get in, and how chatting uses them up. For example, 1 token per character typed, burned or sent back to the owner. Every room can have its own economy.

## 6. Friends

The Friends tab in your wallet is your address book: people you've paid, called, chatted with or followed. A friend only needs a name; if they have a token, their row shows how many you hold, with a button to enter their room or buy in. Message, call or pay anyone in one tap.

[Get bWalletX for Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta and some room rules are still being rolled out. Tokens can lose all value. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Sign in with Gmail

Make a bWalletX wallet with your Gmail account and it comes with a verified name. People pay you at it, hold it as a token and use it to get into your chat room.

you@gmail.com→
you.gmail@bwalletx.com→
$YOU.GMAIL

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer.

- Tap Create account, then Continue with Google.

- Pick your Gmail account on Google's own sign-in page.

- Back in bWalletX, your name and picture are filled in. Choose a password and save your 12-word recovery phrase.

- Claim `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`. It's free.

Already have a wallet? Use Restore with your 12 words and Continue with Google to bring the same name back.

## Your name

Your name comes from your Gmail address. Dots don't count and anything after a `+` is ignored, the same way Gmail treats them.

jane.doe@gmail.com`janedoe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

janedoe+shop@gmail.com`janedoe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

jane_doe@googlemail.com`jane-doe.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Only `@gmail.com` and `@googlemail.com` addresses get a `.gmail` name, because only Google can prove who owns them. Work or school Google accounts can still sign in, then pick an ordinary name.

## What you get

### A verified paymail

People send you BSV, tokens and messages at `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`. It's marked verified, and nobody else can claim it.

### Your own token and room

Turn the name into $YOURNAME.GMAIL, a BSV-21 token with your Google picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room.

### Your picture

Your Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

## What Google shares

bWalletX asks Google for three things only: your email address, your name and your profile picture. It never sees your Google password and can't read your email, contacts or files. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; Google has nothing to do with them.

Signing in with Google proves the name. Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Sign in with Google and X are in bWalletX. The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX on iPhone

Apple only allows App Store apps on iPhone, and the App Store edition (bWallet) can’t trade. Until there’s a better route, bWalletX on iPhone is a web app: the full wallet, installed from Safari onto your Home Screen. Read [where your keys are](#keys) before you use it.

Open in Safari→Share→Add to Home Screen

## Install it (one minute)

- On your iPhone, open [web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com) in Safari.

- Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow).

- Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen, then Add.

- Open bWalletX from your Home Screen, and create or restore your wallet there.

## Where your keys are, honestly

### On your phone, not on our servers

The web app is the same non-custodial wallet: your keys are created on the phone, encrypted with your password, and kept in the app’s own storage on the device. We never see them.

### But web storage is more fragile than a real app

iPhone can clear a website’s storage. The installed Home Screen app is much safer than a Safari tab: it has its own storage, the app asks iOS to keep it, and the “7 days unused” rule only counts days you open it. It can still be lost if you delete the Home Screen icon, clear website data in Settings, or don’t open it for a long time. A Safari tab is cleared much sooner, so always use the icon.

### So: it makes you back up first

Before you can receive money, the web app makes you back up. Either save an encrypted backup file (locked with your wallet password) to Files or email it to yourself, or write down your recovery phrase on paper and confirm three of the words. Keep the password with the file; with either backup you can restore the wallet in any bWallet or bWalletX, on any device. Every month it checks you still have it.

It’s still a beta: keep small amounts in it.

## What’s different from Android

### The same wallet

Tokens, the Exchange and Strategies, names, chat rooms, agent accounts and the b agent all work, and the same recovery phrase works in every edition.

### A few phone features are limited

No Face ID unlock: you use your password. Pairing the [CLI](https://bwalletx.com/cli) works while the app is open on screen.

## Prefer the App Store?

bWallet is our App Store edition: send, receive, tokens, names and rooms, with the Market to browse. It’s coming to the App Store; [join the waitlist](https://www.bwallet.space/#waitlist) to hear when it’s out.

[Open web.bwalletx.com](https://web.bwalletx.com)
[Other devices](https://bwalletx.com/get)

Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

One script tagExtension · Phone · WebNo API keys

await bWalletX.signIn({ challenge, pairing })`

# Connect with bWalletX. One script, no API keys.

BRC-100window.CWIWallet discovery

Your page talks straight to the user's wallet. Nothing passes through our servers.

`<!-- 1. add the script -->
<script src="https://bwalletx.com/connect.js"></script>

// 2. connect
const { wallet } = await bWalletX.connect();

// 3. pay, sign, mint (BRC-100)
await wallet.createAction({
description: 'Buy a pixel',
outputs: [{ lockingScript, satoshis: 1000 }],
});`

bWalletX Strategy spec

# One file format for every trading strategy.

Plain-language goalsHard limitsPublic listing spec

The wallet checks the limits before it signs anything. Write one, build a tool, or sell yours on the Exchange.

`"format": "bwalletx.strategy/1",
"goals": "Build a position slowly.
Never chase a pump.",
"rules": {
"actions": ["buy"],
"maxPerTradeUsd": 2,
"maxPerDayUsd": 10,
"maxTotalUsd": 200,
"stop": { "holdTokens": 100000 }
},
"spec": { "risk": "Medium" }`

# Make something. Mint it.

Minting puts your thing on Bitcoin SV. After that it’s yours: you can sell it, send it to a friend, or let people collect it. All from the Mint button in bWalletX.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

## What you can make

### Art & photos

One of a kind, or a numbered collection.

A painting you photographed, sold as a single piece. Or 50 numbered prints of your best shot.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Music

Tracks fans own and play in their wallet.

Release a single as 100 copies. Fans keep it, play it, and can pass it on.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Videos & films

Clips, shorts or a whole film.

A short film, a behind-the-scenes clip, or episode one of your series.

Straight from the Mint button. Up to 10 MB per file.

### Books & PDFs

Ebooks, zines, guides, reports.

A zine, a recipe book, or a guide you wrote, as a PDF, ebook or text file.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A website

A one-page site, on chain for good.

A one-page portfolio, a wedding page, or a manifesto that nobody can take down.

Straight from the Mint button, as one HTML page.

### Tickets & passes

Entry to your chatroom, event or site.

Sell 30 passes to your private chatroom, or tickets to a gig. Holding one lets you in.

Straight from the Mint button.

### A coin or memecoin

Your own token, fixed supply.

A coin for your club, your community or just for fun. You pick the name and how many exist.

Straight from the Mint button.

### Contracts

Agreements both sides sign.

A deal with a client: half up front, half when the work is delivered.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### Trading strategies

Package a strategy others can buy.

A rule like “buy this token weekly, stop at $50”, packaged so others can buy and run it.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

### An app

List your bApp with its own token.

You built an app. List it in the wallet’s Apps tab with a token of its own.

b, the wallet’s AI assistant, drafts it with you.

## What it costs

### Usually well under a cent for a photo

You pay the Bitcoin SV network to store your file, so the price depends on its size. A typical photo costs a fraction of a cent. A 1 MB file is about two cents. A full 10 MB video is about 20 cents. bWalletX adds a 1% fee on top of the network fee. Starting a new collection takes one extra transaction, so it roughly doubles the cost of that first mint.

The wallet shows the exact price in dollars before you confirm. Prices here assume BSV at about $20 and the wallet’s standard network fee; they move with the BSV price. The limit is 10 MB per file; the wallet can shrink a big photo for you.

## Contracts and new kinds of instruments

A contract in bWalletX is an agreement that both sides sign. Once it is locked on chain, it pays out by its own rules: money goes where the contract says, when the contract says. b, the wallet’s AI assistant, helps you draft it. It asks who it’s between, what each side agrees to, the price and the dates.

### Please read this

Anything that works like an investment, such as shares, bonds or a pension, may be regulated where you live. You are responsible for following the law. bWalletX is a wallet: it does not offer investments, and it can’t tell you whether something you make is allowed. If in doubt, ask a lawyer before you mint or sell it.

## Questions

### Is it permanent?

Yes. Inscriptions on Bitcoin SV can’t be deleted. So don’t mint anything you don’t own, and nothing illegal.

### Who owns it?

Whoever holds it in their wallet. When you mint, that’s you. Your keys stay on your device; we can’t move your things.

### Can I sell it?

Yes. List it on the [Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange) tab, set a price in dollars, and buyers pay in BSV. You can also just send it to someone.

### Does it work on my phone and in Chrome?

Yes. bWalletX runs on [Android](https://bwalletx.com/android), [iPhone](https://bwalletx.com/iphone) and as a [Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension). Contracts, strategies and apps need the full bWalletX (with b, the assistant).

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta: test with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

---

Source: https://bwalletx.com/pnee

# PNEEs · Penny Stablecoins

Digital pennies on BSV. Each PNEE is one US cent (ticker $PNEE), backed only by BSV locked in public vaults. Notes are cash: spend them, send them, price things in them. No bank account behind them, no co-signer on your transfers, nobody who can freeze them.

Lock BSV→Mint PNEEs→Spend them

## How it works

### Notes are pennies that add up

One PNEE unit is one cent. A $10 note is just 1,000 of them together; they split and combine like any token, and the wallet shows dollars. PNEE is an ordinary BSV-21 token, so any 1Sat-compatible wallet can hold it.

### Vaults: lock BSV, mint notes

Anyone can lock BSV in a vault contract and mint notes against it, up to a tenth of its value to start (10x collateral). They keep their BSV and its upside; to unlock it, they hand the notes back. BSV went from $11 to $20 in three months, so we started very safe: a vault survives an 85% fall in BSV.

### Liquidation keeps every note backed

If BSV falls so far that a vault drops below 150%, anyone may repay its notes and take its BSV at a 10% discount. The price comes from 3 of 5 signers, using the median, with fresh timestamps.

### No interest

Notes are cash, like banknotes: holders don’t earn interest and vault owners don’t pay a yearly fee. The vault owner’s reward is spendable dollars without selling their BSV.

## PNEEs and MNEE

PNEEsMNEE

Backed byBSV locked in public vaults, visible on chainUS dollars held by a company

Can your transfer be blocked?No: notes move freelyEvery transfer is co-signed by MNEE’s server

If BSV crashesProtected by 10x collateral and liquidationsUnaffected (dollar reserves)

## The mainnet pilot (live)

PNEEs are live on BSV mainnet in a small, capped pilot: a $5 cap per vault and $10 in total.

- Token: [1599c4e49a…_0](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/1599c4e49a28c7791295f50613e1545aa9246dd592ae8b8f696b81916a475ae4) (BSV-21, 2 decimals). The whole supply sits in the issuer treasury; notes leave it only when a vault mints.

- First vault: [3a782a53…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/3a782a53ea17fdea202488c7d4e0ca335be85d1663b9a6bfb87e9435245d78f2), 12,500,000 sats of BSV (about $2.54) locked.

- First mint: [de18356c…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/de18356cb0560547d68776941a921c28fe04227b7f9e892ebbefbd1e43a00980), 25 PNEEs, checked against a 3-of-5 price of $20.32.

- First release: [913e2a78…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/913e2a786da02d21b86d4d688e25a3879879ac6e62130cfd0ebacb4657145c5a), 25 PNEE from the treasury to the vault owner.

- First liquidation (5 Oct 2026): a small, clearly labelled demo vault ([9f9f5343…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/9f9f53438a8a2463935eadf62bc221f4d035c9e1c55e0376fad801ed6de4a727), 1,000,000 sats, 2 PNEEs) whose on-chain rules allow liquidation below 1100%, so it could be shown at the real price. At a 3-of-5 median of $20.09 the vault stood at 1000%. The liquidator burned the 2 PNEEs ([640acc97…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/640acc972dd08f95b027d4ddc58bf39ce1c45782c73d15300b92f590dd4e0d29)) and liquidated the vault ([7d496a59…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/7d496a59ef82e3dfbb763f52cae5063535c4273a9812ac643714da093400be4e)): the contract paid the liquidator the debt plus the 10% discount (106,558 sats after the fee) and returned the rest, 890,493 sats, to the vault owner. Real vaults use 150%; the main pilot vault is at about 1000% and is not liquidatable.

## What we haven’t solved yet

### Honest trust model

The vault contract can’t yet see by itself that notes were really burned, so for now the issuer (bCorp) co-signs note releases and burns, in public on chain. The five price signers are run by us during the pilot. Both are fine for a few dollars and not for real money: independent price signers and an on-chain burn check come before any meaningful amount.

[Exchange › Bonds](https://bwalletx.com/exchange)
[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)

PNEEs are an experiment. Don’t put in more than you can lose. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# PNEEs · Penny Stablecoins

Digital pennies on BSV. Each PNEE is one US cent (ticker $PNEE), backed only by BSV locked in public vaults. Notes are cash: spend them, send them, price things in them. No bank account behind them, no co-signer on your transfers, nobody who can freeze them.

Lock BSV→Mint PNEEs→Spend them

## How it works

### Notes are pennies that add up

One PNEE unit is one cent. A $10 note is just 1,000 of them together; they split and combine like any token, and the wallet shows dollars. PNEE is an ordinary BSV-21 token, so any 1Sat-compatible wallet can hold it.

### Vaults: lock BSV, mint notes

Anyone can lock BSV in a vault contract and mint notes against it, up to a tenth of its value to start (10x collateral). They keep their BSV and its upside; to unlock it, they hand the notes back. BSV went from $11 to $20 in three months, so we started very safe: a vault survives an 85% fall in BSV.

### Liquidation keeps every note backed

If BSV falls so far that a vault drops below 150%, anyone may repay its notes and take its BSV at a 10% discount. The price comes from 3 of 5 signers, using the median, with fresh timestamps.

### No interest

Notes are cash, like banknotes: holders don’t earn interest and vault owners don’t pay a yearly fee. The vault owner’s reward is spendable dollars without selling their BSV.

## PNEEs and MNEE

PNEEsMNEE

Backed byBSV locked in public vaults, visible on chainUS dollars held by a company

Can your transfer be blocked?No: notes move freelyEvery transfer is co-signed by MNEE’s server

If BSV crashesProtected by 10x collateral and liquidationsUnaffected (dollar reserves)

## The mainnet pilot (live)

PNEEs are live on BSV mainnet in a small, capped pilot: a $5 cap per vault and $10 in total.

- Token: [1599c4e49a…_0](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/1599c4e49a28c7791295f50613e1545aa9246dd592ae8b8f696b81916a475ae4) (BSV-21, 2 decimals). The whole supply sits in the issuer treasury; notes leave it only when a vault mints.

- First vault: [3a782a53…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/3a782a53ea17fdea202488c7d4e0ca335be85d1663b9a6bfb87e9435245d78f2), 12,500,000 sats of BSV (about $2.54) locked.

- First mint: [de18356c…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/de18356cb0560547d68776941a921c28fe04227b7f9e892ebbefbd1e43a00980), 25 PNEEs, checked against a 3-of-5 price of $20.32.

- First release: [913e2a78…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/913e2a786da02d21b86d4d688e25a3879879ac6e62130cfd0ebacb4657145c5a), 25 PNEE from the treasury to the vault owner.

- First liquidation (5 Oct 2026): a small, clearly labelled demo vault ([9f9f5343…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/9f9f53438a8a2463935eadf62bc221f4d035c9e1c55e0376fad801ed6de4a727), 1,000,000 sats, 2 PNEEs) whose on-chain rules allow liquidation below 1100%, so it could be shown at the real price. At a 3-of-5 median of $20.09 the vault stood at 1000%. The liquidator burned the 2 PNEEs ([640acc97…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/640acc972dd08f95b027d4ddc58bf39ce1c45782c73d15300b92f590dd4e0d29)) and liquidated the vault ([7d496a59…](https://whatsonchain.com/tx/7d496a59ef82e3dfbb763f52cae5063535c4273a9812ac643714da093400be4e)): the contract paid the liquidator the debt plus the 10% discount (106,558 sats after the fee) and returned the rest, 890,493 sats, to the vault owner. Real vaults use 150%; the main pilot vault is at about 1000% and is not liquidatable.

## What we haven’t solved yet

### Honest trust model

The vault contract can’t yet see by itself that notes were really burned, so for now the issuer (bCorp) co-signs note releases and burns, in public on chain. The five price signers are run by us during the pilot. Both are fine for a few dollars and not for real money: independent price signers and an on-chain burn check come before any meaningful amount.

# Push notifications

Never miss a message. Real push notifications for messages, mentions, payments and calls are being built now and rolling out soon, on your phone, the web wallet and the Chrome extension.

Coming sooniPhoneAndroidWebChrome extension

## How it works today

While the app is open, it checks for new messages, replies, mentions and payments every 90 seconds and shows a notification on your phone. When the app is closed, nothing arrives yet. On the web wallet and the Chrome extension you see the bell inside the app only.

## What's coming

### iPhone

Apple Push Notifications, so alerts arrive with the app closed.

### Android

Firebase Cloud Messaging, so alerts arrive with the app closed.

### Web wallet and Chrome extension

Web Push, so your browser can tell you even when the tab isn't open.

## What will notify you

- Direct messages from friends, always.

- Group chats: each group has a bell with All, Mentions or Off. Groups start on Mentions, so busy rooms don't buzz you all day.

- Mentions of your `$name`.

- Payments received: BSV and tokens.

- $b answers to your `/b` questions.

- Calls.

## Privacy

By default a notification says who messaged you, not what they wrote, so nothing private shows on your lock screen. If you want message previews, turn them on in Settings. No message text is stored on our push server.

You can turn notifications off per group, per category, or entirely in Settings › Notifications. Your keys never leave your device; notifications don't need them.

## bWalletX and bWallet

Notifications work the same in both editions: bWalletX here, and bWallet, the App Store and Google Play version.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Push notifications are in development and not live yet; this page will be updated as they roll out. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX Social

Social in bWalletX starts with your name. One name does three jobs: it's where people pay you, it's a token people can hold, and it's the key to your chat room. Around it: the Feed, calls, and a wallet that knows your friends.

handle@bwalletx.com→
$HANDLE→
$HANDLE room

## 1. Handles

Your handle is a paymail: an address that looks like an email, such as `yourname@bwalletx.com`. People send you money, tokens and messages to your name instead of a long string of letters and numbers. Claiming one is free.

A wallet has one main name. It can keep older names that still receive, and Settings › Identity lists every one of them, so nothing receives for you without you knowing. You can unlink any of them.

## 2. Sign in with X or Google

Prove who you are, and your name is verified:

### X → `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with X and you get your exact X username, marked as verified. Nobody else can claim it. [How X sign-in works](https://bwalletx.com/x).

### Google → `yourname.gmail@bwalletx.com`

Sign in with a Gmail address and you get a matching verified name. [How Gmail sign-in works](https://bwalletx.com/gmail).

Your X or Google profile picture becomes your wallet's picture too. bWalletX never sees your X or Google password, and your keys never leave your device. If a wallet has a verified name, that name is its main name, token and room. Want a different identity? Add another account.

## 3. Tokenised handles

Turn your name into a token in one tap: $HANDLE for handle@bwalletx.com. It's a BSV-21 token on the Bitcoin SV blockchain, with a fixed supply that starts in your wallet. Its icon is your profile picture.

Anyone can copy a ticker, so bWalletX checks every token's signed creator record. Only the token actually made by that name's owner gets the check mark. Copycats don't.

Personal tokens are social tokens: they're for access and fun, not investments. They don't pay dividends.

## 4. The market

Every user token can be bought and sold in the bWalletX Market. List some of yours for sale at your own price, or buy someone else's to get into their room. Trades settle directly between wallets on chain; bWalletX never holds your tokens or money.

Before a token shows up in other wallets and the Market, its creator pays a one-off indexing deposit to the 1Sat indexer. It's a prepaid balance that pays for the token's transfers, not a fee to bWalletX.

## 5. Chat rooms

Every user token has a chat room. Hold the token, join the room. Inviting someone is as simple as sending them one token.

The room's owner sets its rules: how many tokens you need to hold to get in, and how chatting uses them up. For example, 1 token per character typed, burned or sent back to the owner. Every room can have its own economy.

## 6. Social in your wallet

The Friends tab in your wallet is your address book, with your own $NAME token at the top: people you've paid, called, chatted with or followed. A friend only needs a name; if they have a token, their row shows how many you hold, with a button to enter their room or buy in. Message, call or pay anyone in one tap.

## 7. The Feed

Posts from BSV social apps (bChat, Twetch, Treechat and more) in one Feed: Following, For you and Latest. Post, reply, quote, like, tip the author in sats, or lock BSV behind a post (it stays yours and unlocks at the date shown). Bookmark, mute, block and report are built in.

## 8. Calls

Call anyone with a name, straight from the wallet. Calls are signed by your wallet key, so people know it’s really you; add the person to your friends from the call screen.

[Get bWalletX for Android](https://bwalletx.com/android)
[Chrome extension](https://bwalletx.com/extension)
[All features](https://bwalletx.com/features)

bWalletX is in beta and some room rules are still being rolled out. Tokens can lose all value. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

20 places

## How it works

- Sign in with Google and apply. Use the Google account on your Android phone.

- I read every application and approve testers by hand. If you're in, I add your email to the Google Play test and you'll see your tester code here.

- Join the test on Google Play and install bWallet from there (not the APK from this site).

- Open bWallet, go to Settings › Testing and enter your tester code. The app checks in once a day when you open it.

- Open bWallet every day for 14 days. Use it like you normally would: send a little, receive, try the features.

## What you get

- 0.25 BSV after you first open the app installed from Google Play.

- 0.75 BSV once you've checked in on at least 12 of the 14 days.

- Paid to your own bWallet receive address. I pay each one by hand and you'll see the transaction id here.

## The rules

- One place per person: one Google account, one phone, one wallet. Duplicates get declined.

- Payment never depends on ratings or reviews. Please don't leave a review because of this; Google doesn't allow paid reviews. Report bugs and ideas in the app instead (Settings › Contact and reports).

- I approve applicants, and I can say no or remove a place if something looks wrong.

- 20 places. When they're gone, they're gone.

- What the app sends while you test is in the [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#testers): a random install id, your tester code, whether it came from Google Play, and the app version. Nothing about your keys or money.

# Sign in with X

Make a bWalletX wallet with your X account and it comes with a verified name: your X username. People pay you at it, hold it as a token and use it to get into your chat room.

@yourhandle→
yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com→
$YOURHANDLE

## How to do it

- [Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get) on your phone or computer.

- Tap Create account, then Continue with X.

- Sign in on X's own page and allow access.

- Back in bWalletX, your @handle and picture are filled in. Choose a password and save your 12-word recovery phrase.

- Claim `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`. It's free.

Already have a wallet? Go to Settings › Identity › Connect X or Google. The verified name becomes your wallet's main name, and your older name still receives.

Moving to a new phone? Use Restore with your 12 words and Continue with X to bring the same name back. If the 12 words belong to a different wallet, bWalletX says so and stops, so your name can't end up on the wrong wallet.

## Your name

Your name is your X username in lower case, with `.x` on the end. X allows underscores in usernames and paymail names don't, so an underscore becomes a hyphen.

@b0aseX`b0asex.x@bwalletx.com`

@Jane_Doe`jane-doe.x@bwalletx.com`

One X account gets one name, held by one wallet. If you change your X username later, the name you claimed stays as it was.

## What you get

### A verified paymail

People send you BSV, tokens and messages at `yourhandle.x@bwalletx.com`. It's marked verified, and nobody else can claim it, because only the owner of the X account can sign in as it.

### Your own token and room

Turn the name into $YOURHANDLE, a BSV-21 token with your X picture as its icon. Hold the token, join your room. In Market › Friends it's listed with your x.com link and a tick.

### Your picture

Your X profile picture becomes your wallet's picture, so friends recognise you in chats, calls and payments.

## How it differs from Gmail

It works the same way as [Sign in with Gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail), with two differences. X doesn't give us an email address, so your name comes from your username, not an address. And any X account can get a `.x` name, where only `@gmail.com` addresses get a `.gmail` one.

A wallet holds one verified name. If it already has a `.gmail` name, add another account for your `.x` one.

## What X shares

bWalletX reads three things from X: your username, your display name and your profile picture. It never sees your X password, can't post for you and doesn't read your messages. Your wallet's keys are made on your device and never leave it; X has nothing to do with them.

Signing in with X proves the name. Your 12-word recovery phrase is still the only way to get your money back, so keep it safe.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Sign in with Gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail)
[Social in bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/social)
[Privacy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy)

Sign in with X and Google are in bWalletX (Android APK, Chrome extension, web and iPhone). The App Store and Google Play version, bWallet, doesn't have them yet. They aren't offered for agent accounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# The b agent

The b agent is the AI assistant built into bWalletX. Tap the b in the centre of the top bar to chat with it: it knows how the wallet works, helps you design strategies, and in chat rooms you can call it in with `/b`.

### Looking for agent accounts: AIs with their own wallet?

Separate accounts that an AI runs for you, each with its own budget and its own ghost. [Agent accounts →](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

## Two ways to use it

### Your own key

Add an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter. It stays in secure storage on your device and requests go straight from your phone to that provider. We don't see them. This is the more private option.

### Pay per message

The wallet gets a quote, pays in BSV and gets the answer, with a daily limit. The price is set in US dollars and converted to sats at quote time.

## In chats: /b

Type `/b` followed by your question in a chat room and the b agent answers there, paid in $b.

## What it can do

Explain a feature
Create a strategy
Trade with a strategy
Buy or sell one

It has the wallet's usage guide as its system prompt, so it can explain features. In an agent account it can act, buying and sending, but only through the strategy rules the wallet enforces, never on its own judgement. [How strategies work →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

## Privacy and consent

Before the first message to each provider, a consent sheet shows what is sent (your message and the last 8 turns) and what isn't. You can revoke consent in Settings. The agent refuses input that looks like a recovery phrase or private key, and it has no long-term memory, by design.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Agent accounts](https://bwalletx.com/agents)

The store builds use your own key only. The story so far: [009 The b agent: paid, or your own key](https://bwalletx.com/blog/009-the-b-agent). Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# Agent accounts: every AI gets its own ghost

An agent account is a separate wallet account that an AI runs for you, with its own keys and its own budget. It trades, sends and reports inside the limits you set, and you can stop it or sweep everything back any time.

### Looking for the b agent?

The assistant you chat with inside the wallet is the b agent. [The b agent →](https://bwalletx.com/agent)

Traderrunning
Slow accumulator · cap $20/day
$120.00

Treasurerrunning
Tops up the other agents
$64.25

Reporterread only
Daily summary to chat
$0.00

Scoutstopped
$HANDLE fund · paused by you
$18.90

## The ghost is the agent's face

Make an account an agent account and it gets a pixel ghost in its own colour. It shows on the wallet card when that account is selected and is the account's avatar everywhere: the account menu, Settings and chat. One look tells you which agent you're in.

1st

2nd

3rd

4th

5th

6th

7th

8th

## What an agent account can do

### Spend only its budget

Its balance is all it can ever spend. Fund it from any of your accounts in one tap; your other accounts are never touched.

### Follow a strategy

Agree the rules in plain words, or load a strategy, and it trades by those rules and nothing else. [Strategies →](https://bwalletx.com/strategies)

### Show its work

An activity log lists every action, with links to the transactions. Add labels and an optional daily spending cap in dollars.

### Stop on your word

Stop one agent or Stop all agents. A stopped account refuses every spend until you resume it, and Sweep back moves every token, NFT and all the BSV home.

## Many agents

Run one AI per account, or one across several. A Trader on two strategy accounts, a Treasurer that tops them up, a Reporter that only reads: each sees only the accounts you give it.

## bAgents

bAgents is the home for agents on bWalletX: browse, set up and manage the AIs that run your agent accounts. [agents.bwalletx.com →](https://agents.bwalletx.com)

## Pair a computer, or Claude

The bWalletX CLI runs agent accounts on a laptop or a server. Pair it with your phone so the phone signs every request, or export an agent account's key file to run unattended. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules.

`# install (Node 20+)
npm i -g bwalletx
bwalletx login --account phone # scan the QR in your agent account
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy
bwalletx stop # kill switch
# Claude Code, over MCP
claude mcp add bwalletx -- npx -y bwalletx mcp`

Over MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any agent can manage the agent accounts you give it, within the same limits as the app. An AI can only load strategies on paper: going live is a step you take yourself. [CLI guide →](https://bwalletx.com/cli) · [MCP guide →](https://bwalletx.com/mcp)

## Start in a minute

In bWalletX, open the account menu and tap Add agent account, or go to Settings › Agents. Move in a small budget, give it a strategy, and its ghost appears on the card.

[Get bWalletX](https://bwalletx.com/get)
[Agents in the web wallet](https://web.bwalletx.com/agents)

Agent accounts spend real money: start with small amounts. Questions: [support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com)

# bWalletX CLI

Your wallet and your agents from the command line, on your laptop or a server.

npm i -g bwalletx→
bwalletx login→
bwalletx agent run

## Get started

``npm i -g bwalletx # Node 20+
bwalletx login --account phone # shows a QR: scan it in bWalletX from your agent account``

In bWalletX (5.1.40 or later), open your agent account, then Settings › Paired websites › Scan to connect. Check both screens show the same 4-digit code, choose what the CLI may do and for how long (1, 7 or 30 days), and tap Pair. Your keys never leave the phone.

For a server with no phone around, export a key file instead: Agents › your agent account › Run on a computer › Export for CLI, then `bwalletx key import ./trader.key.json`.

## Commands

``bwalletx accounts # paired and imported agent accounts
bwalletx balance --account trader # BSV and tokens, in dollars
bwalletx price <tokenId>
bwalletx send 1 name@bwalletx.com --account trader
bwalletx buy <tokenId> --max-usd 2 --account phone # cheapest listing, +1% fee, never over the cap
bwalletx strategy load ./slow-accumulator.json --account trader
bwalletx agent run trader # run its strategy unattended
bwalletx log --account trader
bwalletx stop # kill switch: refuse every spend``

## What works today (v0.2)

### Live

Balances, prices, the activity log, sending BSV to an address or paymail, and buying BSV-21 tokens from the Exchange. Strategies run by `agent run` trade for real once you load them live.

### Paired or key file

Paired (`bwalletx login`): the phone checks and signs every request, so bWalletX must be open on that agent account. Key file: runs unattended on a server.

### Coming

Selling, listing and minting from the CLI.

## Your keys stay safe

### Agent accounts only

Only agent accounts can be exported, never your main wallet. The key file is encrypted with a passphrase you choose and stays encrypted on disk.

### Limits

The agent account's balance is the budget. Every spend is checked first: the kill switch, the daily cap, at most 30 spends an hour, then the strategy's rules. Every action is logged.

Free example strategies and the file format: [Strategies](https://bwalletx.com/strategies) · [spec](https://bwalletx.com/strategies/spec). Source: [github.com/b0ase/bwalletx-cli](https://github.com/b0ase/bwalletx-cli) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bwalletx).

[Agent wallet](https://bwalletx.com/agent)
