Source: https://bwalletx.com/blog/015-launchpad

[Development blog](https://bwalletx.com/blog) · 015 · 7 Oct 2026

# Launchpad, and checking what we sign

bWalletX 5.1.74 can buy and sell bonding-curve coins. The wallet now checks every trade the server prepares before it signs anything.

## What Launchpad is

Launchpad is a filter in Market. It lists BlastPad bonding-curve coins and lets you buy and sell them from inside the wallet.

A bonding curve sets the price from how many coins have been sold. The server builds the transaction for each trade and the wallet signs it.

Launchpad is only in bWalletX. The store builds of bWallet carry none of its code or text.

## Confirm before signing

A Buy or Sell tap opens a confirm panel first. It shows the exact token amount, the BSV to the sat, the dollar value, the slippage floor and a line saying trades are final. Nothing is signed until you press Confirm.

Buys have a maximum size. You can only sell once your holdings have loaded.

## The wallet checks the server

A confirm panel only shows what the server tells it. So in 5.1.74 the wallet works out the trade itself and compares.

It reads the pool's state from the transaction data the server sends, runs its own copy of the curve, and rebuilds every output. Then it checks:

- the token output: right token, right amount, going to you;

- the BSV going into the pool;

- 0.70% to the house address and 0.30% to the route;

- the indexing fee, capped;

- that there are no other outputs;

- that the server's quote equals ours;

- that the BSV leaving your wallet is no more than the amount, the indexing fee and 2 sats.

When you sell, the proceeds go to your own account address as a plain output, and that is checked before signing too.

If anything doesn't match, the wallet refuses the plan and releases the pool. We wrote tests for the bad cases: extra outputs, inflated outputs, the wrong token, the wrong amount, the wrong recipient, a short payout and a quote that doesn't match.

The point is simple. A server we run could be wrong or could be broken into. The wallet shouldn't take its word for it.

## Indexing a token you hold

A token only shows up properly once the 1Sat indexer is funded to track it. If the indexer reports a token as inactive or out of funds, the token page now shows an Index $X button to anyone who holds it.

If you hold a token but didn't create it, you pay only the indexing cost. No fee to us.

When you mint your own handle's token and open its chat room, we add $1 on top. That is the only time we charge it. The button says the exact sats and whether the fee is included, and the confirm sheet lists each line and the network fee.

— Richard

Related: [Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/exchange) · [006 Who pays for indexing](https://bwalletx.com/blog/006-paying-for-indexing) · [008 Building the Exchange](https://bwalletx.com/blog/008-the-exchange)

[← 014 One feed for BSV](https://bwalletx.com/blog/014-open-feed)[016 Subscriptions, paid from pots →](https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots)

Source: https://bwalletx.com/blog/016-pots

[Development blog](https://bwalletx.com/blog) · 016 · 7 Oct 2026

# Subscriptions, paid from pots

Subscriptions in bWalletX are paid from a subscription pot: money you set aside for them. We call them pots for short. They are out now in 5.1.76, at Settings › Pots. Free, with billing off.

## What a pot is

If you use Monzo you know the idea. A pot is money set aside from your main balance, with a name: "Rent", "bChat", "Netflix".

In bWalletX a pot is its own small account, with its own keys and balance. It works the same way as agent accounts, with a stop button and a log of everything it paid.

## Regular payments

You can add a regular payment to a pot: who to pay, how much, how often, when to start and, if you like, how many times.

Payments are made when you open the app, on or after each date. If you don't open it for a while, it catches up when you do: up to three missed payments, and it asks you before paying more than that.

Pause takes one tap and needs no confirmation. Resume is one tap too, and the payments you missed while paused are skipped, not paid. Cancel stops a payment for good.

Your phone reminds you the day before a payment is due, even with the app closed. If a pot is running low, or a payment fails, you get a notice.

## The most you can lose

A pot can only spend what is in it. The pot balance is the most you can ever lose to a payment, a bug or a bad payee. The pot screens say so when you set one up.

Each pot also has a daily cap. By default it is set from the pot's largest payment, with room for a three-payment catch-up, so a fault can't empty it in one day.

Each payment is saved on the phone before it is sent. If the app crashes halfway, it sends the same saved payment again rather than making a new one, so nothing is paid twice.

Your keys stay on your phone. We looked at holding pot keys on a server so payments could go out with the app closed, and said no. That would make us custodians of your money.

## The store edition

bWallet, the edition in the App Store and Play Store, has pots and regular payments to people (a $handle or paymail). Subscriptions to apps and services are in bWalletX only.

## No charge

Pots are free. We have written down a possible charge of 1 cent a day for later, but it is switched off, and it will never be on in the store builds. If it ever comes on, pausing, cancelling and taking your money out of a pot will still be free.

## Next

After that, we want payments that go out on time with the app closed, still without us holding keys. The wallet would sign a few payments in advance, each locked with nLockTime so it can't be broadcast before its date. That is the next step, not part of 5.1.76.

— Richard

# Sign in with bWalletX, and the Lounge

bChat now has one gold button to sign in with your wallet. Every account starts in the bWallet Lounge.

## One button

bChat's sign-in page used to offer a long list. Now there is one gold bWalletX button at the top, with X and Google under it and the rest under "More ways".

The button works three ways:

- with the bWalletX extension in Chrome or Brave;

- with bWalletX on your phone, by scanning a QR code;

- with the web wallet at web.bwalletx.com.

bChat sends a challenge, your wallet signs it with your identity key, and bChat checks the signature. No password. If your wallet already has a bChat account, you land in that account instead of a new one.

## Rooms and share links

Token rooms on bChat now offer bWalletX first. Room share cards and offer emails used to say HandCash only; now they say you can sign in with bWalletX.

We also fixed a rough edge. If you weren't signed in and opened an open room like the Lounge, you got "Unauthorized". Now you get a sign-in prompt.

## The Lounge

The bWallet Lounge is the room where everyone who uses the wallet can talk to each other and to us. Every account is now in it by default. If you leave, you stay left; we don't add you back.

You can get there at [bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE](https://www.bitcoinchat.online/room/LOUNGE), or from the b in the middle of the bwalletx.com navbar.

— Richard

# 1 BSV for testing bWallet on Android

Google needs 12 people to test bWallet for 14 days before it can go on the Play Store. We are paying 1 BSV for that time.

## Why we are paying

Google won't let a new developer account publish an app on the Play Store until at least 12 people have tested it for 14 days in a row.

We don't have 12 people sitting around with Android phones. So we are paying for their time: 1 BSV each.

## How it works

- Go to [bwalletx.com/testers](https://bwalletx.com/testers), sign in with the Google account on your Android phone and apply.

- I read every application and approve testers by hand. If you're in, I add your email to the Google Play test and your tester code appears on the page.

- Join the test on Google Play and install bWallet from there, not the APK from this site.

- Open bWallet, go to Settings › Testing and enter your code. The app checks in once a day when you open it.

## What you get

- 0.25 BSV after you first open the app installed from Google Play.

- 0.75 BSV once you've checked in on at least 12 of the 14 days.

It goes to your own bWallet receive address. I pay each one by hand and the transaction id shows on the page.

## The rules

- Payment never depends on ratings or reviews. Please don't leave a review because of this; Google doesn't allow paid reviews. Report bugs in the app instead, under Settings › Contact and reports.

- I can say no, or remove a place if something looks wrong.

- There are 20 places.

While you test, the app sends a random install id, your tester code, whether it came from Google Play, and the app version. That's in the [privacy policy](https://bwalletx.com/privacy#testers).

— Richard

[Development blog](https://bwalletx.com/blog) · 019 · 7 Oct 2026

# Blur slurs, show swearing

The bChat feed and bWalletX now blur slurs behind a tap. Swearing is shown. Nothing is deleted.

## What we changed

The feed reads posts from Twetch, Treechat, Peck, Fwetch and bChat. Some of them contain slurs. We needed a rule.

Our first version hid slurs and had a setting to blur strong language. We changed it a day later. Now, in bChat and bWalletX:

- A post with a slur is blurred, with a "Show anyway" button on that post.

- A display name with a slur is blurred. Tap it to see it. The @handle next to it stays visible.

- Swearing is shown as written.

- There is no 18+ switch to find in Settings.

## Why

Swearing is part of how people talk, so we leave it alone.

Slurs are different. Most people don't want one in front of them without warning, so we put a blur over it and let you decide.

## Nothing is deleted

Every post is on-chain. A filter only changes what you see in our apps. The post is still there and any other app can show it. The "Why blurred?" note says exactly that.

The feed API returns names as they were posted, so each app makes its own choice. The embeddable feed for other sites still drops posts with slurs.

## The store edition

bWallet, the version in the App Store and Google Play, is stricter because the stores require it. Slurs are hidden with no reveal, those names show as "Hidden name", and strong language is blurred.

— Richard

[Development blog](https://bwalletx.com/blog) · 020 · 7 Oct 2026

# Sign in with X

bWalletX can make a wallet from your X account. You get your X username as a verified paymail, b0asex.x@bwalletx.com for example, with your picture, a token and a room.

## What it does

On Create account there is a Continue with X button. You sign in on X's own page, come back to the wallet, and your @handle and picture are already filled in. You still choose a password and save a 12-word recovery phrase. Then you claim the name.

The name is your X username in lower case with `.x` on the end. @b0aseX becomes `b0asex.x@bwalletx.com`. Underscores become hyphens, because paymail names can't have them.

Wallets made before this can do the same from Settings › Identity › Connect X or Google. The verified name becomes the main name, and the old one still receives.

## How the proof works

We run the sign-in ourselves, on the same server as the paymail. Before the wallet opens X, it makes a random secret and sends us only its hash. When X sends you back, we seal your X account into a ticket tied to that hash. The ticket is no use without the secret, and the secret never leaves your device.

To register a `.x` name, the wallet has to show both. So only the person who signed in as @b0aseX can claim `b0asex.x`, and one X account means one wallet.

From X we read your username, display name and picture. We don't ask to post and we don't read messages. X has nothing to do with your keys.

## What went wrong first

On iPhone we first opened x.com in the browser. The X app grabbed the link, its own browser broke X's "Sign in with Google" page, and its "Open bWalletX" button did nothing. It now uses an in-app Safari sign-in sheet that returns straight to the wallet.

On the web wallet, sign-in opened a new tab and ended on a "you're signed in" page with no way back. It now signs in in the same tab and returns to web.bwalletx.com.

Restoring with 12 words and Continue with X could have put a verified name on the wrong wallet. Now the wallet checks the phrase against the name first, on the device, and stops if they don't match.

## Where it is

In bWalletX: the Android APK, the Chrome extension, the web app and iPhone. Not in bWallet, the App Store and Google Play edition, until app review is settled. Not for agent accounts either; an agent posting as someone's X account needs its own design.

How-to page: [bwalletx.com/x](https://bwalletx.com/x).

— Richard

Related: [Sign in with X](https://bwalletx.com/x) · [Sign in with Gmail](https://bwalletx.com/gmail) · [004 Names, handles and paymail](https://bwalletx.com/blog/004-names-and-paymail) · [005 Personal tokens and token rooms](https://bwalletx.com/blog/005-personal-tokens-and-rooms)

# Privacy Policy

bWalletX (Beta) · Effective 6 October 2026

bWalletX is published by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd and is based on the open-source Yours Wallet (MIT licence).
It is not made, reviewed or endorsed by the Yours Wallet authors. This policy covers bWalletX (the full-feature
app, Chrome extension and web wallet) and bWallet, the edition on the App Store and Google Play.

## Summary

bWalletX is non-custodial: your private keys and recovery phrase never leave your device, and we can't move your
money. To run chat, names, contacts and calls, our own service (bit-sign, operated by The Bitcoin Corporation
Ltd) keeps the data listed under
[What our service keeps](#service), linked to your wallet's identity key. If you use bChat on a
phone, our push server also keeps your device's push token and notification settings so it can notify you (see
[Notifications](#push)). We use all of this only to run those features. We don't collect your email
(unless you choose Continue with Google), phone number, location, advertising identifiers, analytics or crash
reports, and we don't track you, sell your data or use it for advertising.

## What stays on your device

-
Your private keys and recovery phrase, encrypted with a key derived from your password and stored in the iOS
Keychain (this device only, excluded from iCloud and device backups) or in Android storage encrypted with an
Android Keystore key (excluded from Google backups).

-
If you turn on Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint unlock, a key to unlock your wallet is sealed behind your
device's biometrics. Your biometric data itself is handled by the operating system and is never available to
the app.

- Settings, recent sites and apps you open, chat history cached for bChat, and local caches.

## What the app sends over the network

To work as a wallet, the app connects to these third-party services, all over HTTPS:

-
Wallet storage: by default, your wallet's transaction records (outputs, transactions and related
metadata, not your private keys) are synced to a remote wallet storage service operated by 1Sat
(`wallet.1sat.app`). You can change the storage provider in Settings → Wallet Backup.

-
Blockchain services: address, balance, transaction and token lookups, and transaction broadcasts, go to
BSV indexing services (1Sat APIs). Some address-history lookups (when you move funds in from another wallet),
transaction checks and the BSV price history use the WhatsOnChain API, and transaction links open on
WhatsOnChain. The BSV price comes from public price feeds.

- Wallet messaging: wallet-to-wallet messages use `messagebox.1sat.app`.

-
Market, Media, Apps and Chat: trending tokens, collections, listings and ordinal media are loaded from
1Sat indexing and content services (ORDFS). The Apps tab lists bApps such as bChat, bMovies and bWriter; bChat
and other bApps you open talk to their own services, which receive what you send them.

-
Names and payments to names: when you send to a $handle, paymail or OpNS name, or look up your own
name, the app asks 1Sat indexers (including OpNS), bit-sign and the paymail service of the address's domain
(for example HandCash for `@handcash.io`) to resolve that name to a payment destination. Those
services see the name being looked up.

-
Market and Chat: token and NFT listings, media and token rooms are loaded from 1Sat indexers. The
Market's safety filter runs as part of that loading; if you use Report, the item is hidden on your device and,
where a review service is configured, the item reference is sent to us for review.

-
Feed: public on-chain posts are loaded from a public bmap indexer and from our own bChat indexer
(`push.bwalletx.com/feed`). Posting puts your post on the public blockchain.

-
$b assistant (optional): nothing is sent until you allow it in the app. In bWallet from the App Store
and Google Play, $b uses your own AI provider key (Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter) and your message and the
recent conversation go straight from your phone to that provider. In bWalletX's pay-per-message mode, they go
to our server (bitcoinchat.online), which passes them to Anthropic; our server also sees the payment's
transaction id and your bChat sign-in, and Anthropic does not. Your keys, balances, addresses, contacts, chats
and files are never sent. You can withdraw consent in Settings › b agent.

-
Websites you open in the in-app browser receive the requests you make and the responses you approve.
They're governed by their own privacy policies.

These services see your IP address and the public blockchain data needed to answer each request. Blockchain
transactions are public by nature.

## What our service keeps

Chat, names, contacts and calls run on bit-sign (`bitcoinchat.online`), operated by The Bitcoin
Corporation Ltd. When you use those features it stores:

- Your identifiers: your wallet's identity key, your $handle and your paymail name.

- Your name: the display name you choose.

- Messages: chat-room and direct messages you send, and room posts.

-
Contacts: the contacts, friends and blocked users you keep in the app (not your phone's address book).

- Other content you create: bookmarks, and items you report for review.

-
Wallet details for rooms and tickets: your wallet addresses and the token holdings needed to check
access to token rooms and tickets.

Calls connect your device directly to the other person's; the service only helps the two devices find each other
and doesn't record calls. All of this is used only to provide these features. It is not shared with third
parties except the hosting providers that run the service, and it is never used for advertising or tracking. You
can delete your account and this data from Settings (Delete account), or by contacting us.

## Verified identity (KYC certificates)

Identity verification is optional. If you choose to verify, you are sent to bit-sign, which uses Veriff to check
your identity document. bit-sign and Veriff keep the verification record under their own privacy policies.
bit-sign then issues a private certificate that is stored in your wallet on your device. bWalletX does not
upload that certificate anywhere by itself: you choose which details, if any, to reveal to an app or service,
and only when you approve it.

## Continue with X or Google (bWalletX only)

If you choose Continue with X or Continue with Google when creating an account, you sign in on X or Google in
your browser and our sign-in service (the bWalletX paymail server, run by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd) receives
your X @name or Gmail address, your display name and your profile photo from them. The app uses these to fill in
your name and photo and, if you claim it, to register a verified paymail such as
`yourname.x@bwalletx.com`. We keep that registration so the paymail keeps working. We don't receive
your X or Google password, and we don't post anything or read anything else from your account. This option isn't
in bWallet from the App Store and Google Play.

## Notifications

On-device alerts. If you allow notifications, the app shows local alerts about incoming transactions.
They're generated on your device.

Push notifications (bChat). When you're signed in to bChat, the app registers your device with our push
server, `push.bwalletx.com`, run by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd on a server we rent from Hetzner, so
you can be told about room mentions and direct messages while the app is closed. On a phone this is on by
default once you sign in to bChat, and your phone asks for permission first; in the web wallet and Chrome
extension it stays off until you turn it on. To do this the app sends:

- the device push token issued by your phone (or, in a browser, the Web Push subscription);

- the platform (iOS, Android, web or extension), the app (bWallet or bWalletX) and its bundle id;

- the bChat handle the device belongs to (your bChat sign-in);

-
your notification preferences: message previews, quiet hours and your time zone, which kinds of alerts you
want, and per-room settings (All, Mentions or Off).

We use this only to send you those notifications. The notification itself is delivered through Google Firebase
Cloud Messaging (Android), Apple Push Notification service (iPhone) or your browser's push service, which
receive the push token and the notification.
Message previews are off by default: a notification then says only that you have something new, without
the message text. If you turn previews on, the message text passes through those services to show it on your
screen.

Turn push off or change previews, quiet hours and alerts in Settings › Notifications › Push notifications, or in
your phone's notification settings. Turning push off, signing out of bChat or switching to another account
removes this device's registration from our push server; uninstalling the app makes its push token stop working.

## Testing waitlist (this website)

If you join the testing waitlist on this website, we collect your email address, the phone platform you chose
(iPhone, Android or Either), the time you signed up, and your browser's user-agent string (to help spot abuse).
This is stored by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd in our own database and is used only to invite you to test bWallet
and send testing updates. We do not sell it or share it for marketing. You can unsubscribe from any email, or
ask us to delete your entry at any time using the contact details below.

## Paid testers programme and tester check-ins

If you apply at [bwalletx.com/testers](https://bwalletx.com/testers), you sign in with Google and we keep
your Google-verified email address, name and profile photo, the Android phone model you type, the X or GitHub
name you give (optional), the BSV address you want to be paid to, the time you applied and your IP address (to
spot duplicate applications). It is stored by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd on our server
(`push.bwalletx.com`, Hetzner) and used only to run the programme: approving testers, adding your email
to the Google Play test list, and paying you.

Tester check-ins. Only in the Google Play build, and only after you enter your tester code (or email) in
Settings › Testing, the app sends one check-in a day while it is open: a random install id made on your
phone, your tester code or email, which app store installed it (so we know it came from Google Play) and the app
version. It sends nothing about your keys, addresses, balances or activity. Unlink in Settings › Testing to
stop. Payment never depends on ratings or reviews. Ask us to delete your tester record at any time.

## Your choices

- You can delete your account and the data our service keeps from Settings (Delete account).

- You can delete all app data on your device by signing out in Settings, or by uninstalling the app.

- You can turn biometric unlock off from the lock screen at any time.

-
You can turn push notifications and message previews off in Settings › Notifications, and remove this device's
push registration by signing out of bChat.

- You can withdraw consent for the $b assistant in Settings › b agent.

- You can change the remote wallet storage provider in Settings → Wallet Backup.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13.

## Changes

We'll post changes to this policy on this page, and in the source repository at
[github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile](https://github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile).

## Contact

The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd:
[support@bwalletx.com](mailto:support@bwalletx.com), or open an issue at
[github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile/issues](https://github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile/issues).
